ProtT5 Glycosylation Prediction — Interpretation Report

Source: ProtT5_glycosylation_clean_pipeline.ipynb  |  Embeddings: ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 • 1024-dim  |  Task: binary protein-level glycosylation classification

1. Dataset

Proteins from UniProt/Swiss-Prot were split into two mutually exclusive classes using the Glycosylation column:

  • Positive (glycosylated): Glycosylation column is populated (notna)
  • Negative (not glycosylated): Glycosylation column is empty (NaN)

Duplicate protein names were removed within each class and overlaps discarded. This labelling is identical to the Ankh and ESM2 glycosylation pipelines.

Figure 1. Class distribution. Glycosylated proteins represent 21.8% of the dataset.

Class imbalance note: PR-AUC (Average Precision) is the primary metric. A random classifier achieves PR-AUC ≈ 0.218. Imbalance is corrected via balanced class weights (LR) and BCEWithLogitsLoss pos_weight (MLP).

2. Methods

2.1 Embeddings

ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 (1024-dimensional) embeddings were loaded from a pre-built cache. Two global representations were evaluated: max pooling and attention pooling. All features z-score normalised (training-set statistics only).

2.2 Classifiers

ModelArchitecture / SettingsImbalance handling
Logistic RegressionL2, max_iter=5000, n_jobs=-1class_weight="balanced"
MLP (PyTorch) Linear(1024→512)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→Linear(512→256)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→Linear(256→1), Adam lr=1e-3, 30 epochs, batch=64 BCEWithLogitsLoss pos_weight=neg/pos

80/20 stratified train/test split, seed 42.

5. Interpretation

5.1 MLP vs Logistic Regression

MLP attn PR-AUC: 0.9358  |  MLP max PR-AUC: 0.9201
LR attn PR-AUC: 0.9060  |  LR max PR-AUC: 0.8875

5.2 Cross-Model Context

ProtT5-XL uses 1024-dim embeddings, between Ankh (768-dim) and ESM-2 (1280-dim). Compare results_glycosylation_ProtT5/, results_glycosylation_ESM2/, and results/ (Ankh) for a three-way comparison on identical data.

5.3 UMAP vs PCA / t-SNE

UMAP preserves global structure better than t-SNE at scale. Convergence across all three projections strengthens visual interpretation. Substantial overlap between classes is expected for protein-level pooled representations.

5.4 Recommendations

  1. Residue-level classifier on ProtT5 token embeddings
  2. 5-fold stratified cross-validation instead of single split
  3. Concatenate max + attention pool (2×1024) as joint feature
  4. Ensemble ProtT5, ESM2 and Ankh embeddings
  5. Fine-tune ProtT5 end-to-end on the glycosylation task
